title: Existence of regular projections
statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every oriented link $L\subset\mathbb R^3$ the set of unit vectors $u\in S^2$ for which the orthogonal projection $\pi_u\colon\mathbb R^3\to u^\perp$ is regular for $L$ is dense in $S^2$; in particular $L$ admits a regular projection, and then the projection has only finitely many double points.
strategy: Consider the tangent-direction map $TL\to S^2$ and the secant maps $(L\times L\setminus\Delta)\to S^2$, $(x,y)\mapsto (y-x)/|y-x|$, and $(L\times L\times L\setminus\Delta_3)\to S^2$: $\pi_u$ fails to be an immersion exactly when $u$ is in the image of the tangent map; a double point fails to be transverse exactly when $u$ is a critical value of the secant map; a triple point occurs exactly when $u$ is in the image of the triple secant map. Sard's theorem for the compact smooth manifolds $L$, $L\times L\setminus\Delta$, $L\times L\times L\setminus\Delta_3$ makes each bad set null (for the triple map the source has dimension $3$ and the target $2$, so the whole image is null), and a finite union of null sets is null, so its complement is dense. Finiteness of the double-point set: for good $u$ it is the preimage of the regular value $[u]$ under the secant map of a compact $2$-manifold, hence discrete and compact, hence finite. AC_omega is inherited from the quoted Sard theorem; a finite-atlas version of Sard on the compact link would remove it and is recorded as a possible strengthening.

references.title: Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society (2024); arXiv:2406.18203v1, sections 2-3
Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
